Hold a flame in front of a bright light. It does not cast a shadow.
A shadow is just the gap where something blocked the light. To make one, you have to be in the way.
A flame is barely in the way. It is thin, hot gas, and light goes straight through it.
Then it does the opposite of blocking. It adds its own light on top.
That is the whole trick. Fire is not an object sitting in the light. Fire is the light.
Try it tonight and you might see something faint. That is not the flame.
That is soot, which is solid, and hot air bending the light as it rises.
So a candle is the one thing in your house that never follows you around.
